problem: UserBar and shared mute shortcuts previously changed guild manual mute while private group capture had separate manual intent. The icon/action could diverge from the actually transmitting group microphone.
contract: An ephemeral audio-control binding exposes exact component call nonce, immutable account/generation, group ID, manual/effective mute, capture conflict and a guarded toggle. This is control routing only, not persistent call ownership or navigation state.

Group local button, UserBar and shared useVoice mute command now reach the same actual group manual intent when no guild/P2P call takes precedence. Unrelated guild moderation does not become authority over private capture.
Dock icon reflects group effective mute; queued-deafen action label uses group manual intent. Undeafen cannot reopen a manually muted group simply because the global guild queued-unmute was false.

Bindings only publish for the initial component account/generation. Account replacement clears control and stale component changes cannot adopt the new owner. Release/toggle require exact nonce; a retained group command never falls through to a replacement group/guild microphone.
Existing capture conflict latch still forces explicit new group unmute when another call ends. Receiving/camera behavior, E2EE admission and exact controller/media ownership stay unchanged.

remaining_acceptance: Real browser/Windows two-client microphone audibility and encrypted media acceptance remain open.

Foreground-only group PTT remains as documented in prior private-audio slice.
Existing non-group P2P global mute-hotkey behavior is not changed by this group-only routing; P2P dock retains its separate dedicated controls.
